proposed_facts.reason: Canonical code confirms identifier fallback, conversion before masking, signed-byte exponent assignment and three immediate writes. Exceptional conversion behavior is appropriately left unspecified.
The count setter updates the cached field and dirty mask without emission. Assertion definitions and the external dispatcher confirm build-dependent enforcement and deferred consumers.
The direct preset arguments match exactly; utc_lod is a Boolean encoded into one bit, not an explicit LOD value.

The selector switch lacks cases above three, preserving the previous tmap in later iterations. DEBUG overlap checking and changed-only emission match the proposal; GXGeometry confirms flush-primitive bookkeeping.

Canonical branches confirm nonuniform validation, immediate order emission, distinct dirty masks, tile fallbacks, uninitialized invalid bump-ST selectors, and conditional update versus unconditional cached-mask emission.

contradictions.reason: Accepted deferral for all four .sdata2 facts: literal uses are supported, but C expressions cannot establish compiled section membership, extent, materialization or ordering.
The universal floating-input wrapping claim is corrected by proposal 0; masking occurs after conversion and does not resolve exceptional conversion semantics.
Unconditional rejection of excessive counts is corrected by proposal 1: the bound is asserted, with assertions disabled when DEBUG is undefined.
Explicit-LOD terminology is corrected by proposal 2 without changing the supported direct-preset interpretation.
Proposal 3 correctly separates the intended count domain from the encoded field and rejects interpreting bpSent zero as an unsent register.
Proposal 4 resolves blanket-validation and deferred-order claims by preserving the actual fallback, assertion and immediate-write branches.
